Milky Way neighborhood — famous nearby systems at their real galactic (l, b, distance) coordinates through gpos. Every star sits at its honest compressed distance (Proxima 0.042 units, Deneb 26.15) so the chart never lies about who's next to whom — no stars render inside the solar diagram. Marker radii are point-scale glyphs (~0.01–0.05 units, physically a star is far smaller) sized by luminosity class so giants still read bigger than dwarfs; pickability comes from the radius-scaled invisible proxy, not inflated geometry.

Two LOD faces per star (see buildStarBodies): the flat point-glow carries the chart view, while a seeded photosphere — granulation, sunspot groups past the activity threshold, rim limb darkening, corona and flares — resolves on approach and spin visibly turns the surface. Planets and stellar companions are real parented bodies with their own eccentric orbits, so every authored system simulates its members rather than decorating the star's glyph.
